https://www.theguardian.com/world/video/.text: 0:56 Kosovo Kosovan lawmaker hurls eggs at the prime minister – video An opposition lawmaker threw eggs at Kosovo's acting prime minister, Albin Kurti, after he told parliament he needed more time to hold talks with other parties before proposing a candidate for speaker following the country's snap election in June. Time Kadrijaj, an Alliance party MP, pulled eggs from her bag and threw them at the prime minister while shouting, 'Shame, shame.' Kosovo has been stuck in a political deadlock for nearly two years. Movies Alexander Skarsgård Gets Bizarre in New Wicker Poster Ahead of Rumored Marvel Role September 16, 2026 By Manoj Chekkilla Alexander Skarsgård ‘s latest look has fans doing a double take. The new poster for his upcoming fantasy rom-com Wicker shows his unusual transformation for the role. The Emmy Award winner has previously been the subject of MCU casting speculation, including reports linking him to Nova . As shared by @DiscussingFilm on X, the exclusive poster shows Skarsgård’s wicker-woven character dipping Olivia Colman in a romantic pose. The rom-com premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2026 and was received well. As of writing, it holds a 91% Tomatometer score on Rotten Tomatoes , based on 23 reviews. Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson wrote and directed the R-rated movie. It adapts Ursula Wills’ short story titled The Wicker Husband. Dev Patel was initially attached to star alongside Colman before being replaced by Skarsgård. What to know about Olivia Colman & Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker The plot revolves around a lonely fisherwoman, played by Colman, who gets fed up with constant mocking from her neighbors. To find a love companion, she takes an unusual approach that causes tension within the conservative village. The film’s official synopsis reads, “On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.” Alongside Colman and Skarsgård, the film also stars Peter Dinklage , Elizabeth Debicki, Marli Siu, Nabhaan Rizwan, Richard E. Grant, and Ben Ashenden. Filming took place in Budapest and was concluded in September last year. Colman also serves as a producer alongside Ed Sinclair and Tom Carver from South of The River, David Michôd and Brad Zimmerman for Yoki, Inc., and Justin Lothrop and Brent Stiefel for Votiv. Distributed by BlackBear Pictures, the 105-minute film is scheduled to be released on October 23, 2026. Manoj Chekkilla Manoj Chekkilla is an Entertainment Writer at Evolve Media, covering film, television, and video games. With over four years of experience across the entertainment and gaming industries, he is known for covering breaking entertainment news, fan reactions, and industry trends. Manoj is particularly interested in stories that explore the intersection of pop culture and entertainment. When he’s not writing, he enjoys watching movies, discovering new series, and playing games. Critics say Trump’s new diesel deal with Moscow is a crushing blow for Ukraine. Critics say Trump’s new diesel deal with Moscow is a crushing blow for Ukraine. Photograph: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Russia Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv blasts peace talks as just ‘smokescreen’ for Trump‘s Russian diesel deal Trump’s announcement a betrayal of Ukraine, Democrats say; Ukraine strikes major datacentre in Russia. What we know on day 1,690 Guardian staff and agencies Fri 9 Oct 2026 21.31 EDT Last modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 23.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukrainian peace negotiators in Miami have been used as a “smokescreen” for a “weak” decision by Donald Trump to lift diesel sanctions on Russia , Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a furious response to the US president’s backflip on Russian sanctions. In a move likely to create a fresh crisis with Washington’s Nato allies, Trump announced the deal with Putin on his Truth Social network, saying it was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared as a result of his decision to go to war with Iran. The Ukrainian president, who flew to Washington last month to plead with US lawmakers to pass tougher sanctions on Russia, said in a statement on Friday that it was “unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners”. “I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other.” Negotiators for the ⁠US, Ukraine and Europe ⁠held ​six ‌hours ‌of talks ‌in Miami on Friday with the aim ‌of reaching agreement ​on ending ​the war ​in ​Ukraine , ​a ‌source ​briefed ​on the talks said. They discussed a postwar economic package for Ukraine and potential new security architecture between Europe and Russia, the source said. President Trump announced the diesel deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Florida to discuss a peace plan. Trump’s announcement was a betrayal of Ukraine, the European allies and US national security, said Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer , top Democrat on the Foreign Relations Committee Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, and senior Democrat senator, Elizabeth Warren. “Enough is enough,” the senators wrote. “The President must end his war with Iran instead of funding Russia’s war machine.” A number of prominent Republicans joined Democrats on Friday to condemn Trump for lifting the diesel sanctions , including congressman Don Bacon, who said the majority of Americans supported Ukraine. “The President’s policies towards Russia and Ukraine are failures. We need moral clarity not moral ambiguity.” Ukraine struck and partly disabled a major datacentre operated by Russian technology company Yandex on Friday in the second such action in successive days. Yandex, which is heavily involved in Russia’s ​AI development, said its data centre in the Kaluga region south-west of Moscow had been struck by Ukrainian drones and partly put out of action. Ukrainian arms maker Firepoint said Kyiv had used its FP-1 one-way attack drones to mount the ⁠strike. Four Ukrainians were arrested in Vienna this week on ⁠suspicion of spying , Austrian interior minister, Gerhard Karner, said on Friday, with Ukrainska ⁠Pravda newspaper saying two ⁠of ​its team were among those detained. Three remain in custody, Karner said, declining ⁠to provide further details because the investigation was ongoing. Austrian news agency APA quoted a ⁠spokeswoman for the Ukrainian embassy in Vienna as saying ​it was awaiting ‌an explanation from the ‌Austrian authorities on the circumstances of and legal grounds ‌for the arrests. The embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russian ⁠forces struck ​three cargo vessels in and ⁠around Ukraine’s Black Sea ports on ⁠Friday , Russia’s defence ministry ​said. The ‌ministry said ‌one vessel was ‌hit in the port of Mykolaiv, another in the port of Chornomorsk and ‌a third, bound for Odesa, in the ​Black Sea. According to the ministry, all three vessels ⁠were being used ​to supply ​the Ukrainian ​military. Reuters could ​not ‌independently verify ​the ​report or the claim. Russian strikes killed three people and wounded at least eight across Ukraine, officials said Friday , as Ukraine struggles to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 50 people over the past three days. A girl runs on Orange Beach, Alabama, as the outer bands of Hurricane Isaias reach shore on 9 October 2026. Photograph: Jen Golbeck/SOPA Images/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen A girl runs on Orange Beach, Alabama, as the outer bands of Hurricane Isaias reach shore on 9 October 2026. Photograph: Jen Golbeck/SOPA Images/Shutterstock Hurricane Isaias Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida and hammers Gulf coast Governors of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida declare states of emergency as a downsized Fema faces first major test Hurricane Isaias - live updates Richard Luscombe in Miami, Uwa Ede-Osifo and agencies Fri 9 Oct 2026 23.56 EDT First published on Fri 9 Oct 2026 21.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Hurricane Isaias crashed into the US Gulf coast on Friday as a dangerous category 2 storm, hammering communities in Alabama and the Florida panhandle with damaging winds, heavy rain, flooding and life-threatening storm surges. The first hurricane of the Atlantic season made landfall near Destin, Florida , the National Hurricane Center said. It had maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (169 kph). The storm weakened to just below major hurricane status before it came ashore. “The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads,” Florida’s governor, Ron DeSantis, said at a news conference, adding flash flooding would be a hazard “throughout the region”. In Pensacola, about 50 miles (80km) west of Destin an Agence France-Presse reporter witnessed howling winds rip the roofs from some homes and businesses, snapping tree branches as the power went out. “Things are flying really fast, and I’ve never seen wind this fast before, so it’s intense, it’s scary,” Jonathan Ramos, a 40-year-old government employee, said from his hotel in Pensacola, where the power went out. “I don’t recommend people coming down here for fun to do this.” President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House late Friday night: “We’re watching it very closely, the hurricane,” adding that it was “under control”. Forecasters had expected Isaias to weaken from its peak earlier on Friday as a major category 3 hurricane because of shifts in wind speed. View image in fullscreen Debris is seen in an intersection as wind and rain from Hurricane Isaias pass through the area in Pensacola, Florida. Photograph: Joe Raedle/Getty Images But even as a weaker storm system, the NHC warned of a ‌life-threatening storm surge affecting the Gulf Coast as dangerous hurricane conditions and flash floods spread inland. The hurricane is expected to cross Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley on the weekend, the ‌agency added. Warnings included a storm surge of up to 7ft (2.1 meters) along the Alabama-Florida line, and powerful wind gusts reaching parts of northern Georgia. In the Florida Panhandle, Isaias’s early impacts also came into view. In Panama city beach, Noaa officials observed a water level 5.4 feet (1.64 meters) above average. About 125 miles west, at the Pensacola city hall, a wind gust up to 102 mph (164km/h) was recorded. Powerful gusts of wind and heavy rainfall appeared to down the canopy of a Crestview gas station on Friday evening, according to a video captured by meteorologist Nick Stewart. The tattered cover hung on top of a filling station. “The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads,” Florida governor Ron DeSantis said at a news conference, adding that flash flooding would be a hazard “throughout the region”. The governors of Mississippi , Alabama and Florida all declared states of emergency ahead of the storm’s arrival, urging some residents of coastal communities to evacuate and many more to prepare for the storm’s likely violent arrival. View image in fullscreen A vehicle drives through a flooded street as a result of Hurricane Isaias in Tarpon Springs, Florida. Photograph: Chris Urso/Reuters Alabama governor Kay Ivey announced shortly before the hurricane made landfall that Donald Trump had approved the emergency declaration for her state. “This will help cut tape for our federal partners to aid in any response,” Ivey said. The Mobile office of the National Weather Service warned parts of Florida could see “extremely dangerous” tornado-like winds. By Friday evening, nearly 500,000 customers had lost power across Alabama and Florida, according to PowerOutage.com. “Things are going to get really, really treacherous,” Jamie Rhome, deputy director for the National Hurricane Center, told the AP. Florida’s national guard deployed roughly 5,000 soldiers and airmen to aid with the response, the AP reported. Some prisons were also evacuating their incarcerated populations. Most flights were grounded at several airports in Florida’s Panhandle. The state guard has deployed about 400 soldiers to assess the hurricane’s damage and assist with route clearance, among other duties. The Florida fish and wildlife conservation commission has readied 10 airboats, 18 shallow-draft boats, nine ATVs and six larger platform vessels in the event of damage or flooding. Uber has also partnered with the state to offer free-round trips, up to $40 each way, to and from state-approved evacuation shelters. View image in fullscreen A fallen tree blocks a street as wind and rain from Hurricane Isaias strikes Pensacola, Florida. Photograph: Joe Raedle/Getty Images Isaias is notable as one of the two latest-forming Atlantic hurricanes on record, tying a record set on 8 October 1905. None of the eight previous named storms of the 2026 Atlantic season intensified above tropical storm status. Ahead of the storm, oil and gas producers shut down a significant share of offshore production in the Gulf, which accounts for almost 15% of crude pumped annually in the US. In a sign of how serious the warnings are, dozens of Waffle Houses in the Florida Panhandle were closed, according to the company’s website. The beloved Southern breakfast chain is known for staying open through severe weather and often is a measuring stick of a storm’s severity. Kelsei Frazier, a Florida native living in Pace who is no stranger to hurricanes, knows all about the Waffle House Index. “We joke because if Waffle House is still open, then you know it’s not a bad hurricane, but all the Waffle Houses that I know of within at least a normal range from us are closed,” said Frazier. “Which is a pretty big deal.” Associated Press contributed reporting. Indonesia: Bali fuel supply delays spark panic buying and hours-long queues Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 14/10/2026 - 23:27 GMT+2 Indonesia's resort island of Bali faced long queues at petrol stations on Wednesday, 14 October, as disrupted fuel deliveries left motorists waiting for hours. … More Queues of motorcycles and cars spilled onto roads across the Indonesian resort island. One Denpasar resident said she had waited about seven hours in the heat to buy petrol . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Officials blamed distribution delays rather than depleted island-wide stocks. Indonesia’s state-owned energy company Pertamina said a tanker’s anchor problem had delayed unloading, while road congestion slowed deliveries to stations. Panic buying added to the pressure, particularly for cheaper, subsidised Pertalite petrol. Bali Governor Wayan Koster urged residents not to panic , saying fuel remained available at storage depots. Pertamina said on Wednesday that an additional 57.9 million litres of petrol were scheduled to arrive in Bali between 14 and 17 October. Deliveries were stepped up around the clock, with 60 stations in Denpasar operating 24 hours a day. Queues persisted despite the additional supplies.
